title: Claude development pipeline configuration
description: Per-repo pipeline contract, read by both the hooks and the skills so they cannot disagree. Two valid shapes: a FULL onboarding config (version, branches, worktrees, commands - what /pipeline-kit:init writes), or a PROTECTION-ONLY config (version plus protectedPaths and/or unprotectedPaths) that configures protected-files.cjs without enrolling the repo in branch enforcement, claims or session registration. The presence of `branches` is what marks a repo as onboarded.

version.description: Schema version. Bump only on a breaking shape change.

kind.description: 'local' means the .scratch/ markdown convention; 'none' disables the ticket gate.

repo.description: owner/name. Cached so hooks never shell out to `gh repo view`.

ghAccount.description: Account to pin per command via GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user <this>). The globally active gh account is mutable and a concurrent session can flip it mid-run.

trunk.description: The single long-lived branch. Under GitHub Flow this is also the default branch, which is what makes PR closing keywords work.

protected.description: Branches the guard refuses direct edits on.

root.description: Repo-relative directory for linked worktrees. Paths outside the blessed root prompt on EnterWorktree.

setup.description: Repo-relative script run once per fresh worktree. Must be idempotent.

commands.description: Verification commands. 'build' and 'test' are the gates a lane runs before claiming a ticket done.

mode.description: 'inline' edits CHANGELOG.md directly and conflicts when branches run in parallel. 'fragments' writes one file per change under dir/ and assembles at release.

dir.description: Fragment directory. Required when mode is 'fragments'.

update.description: What the Land lane does about the repository wiki after a release, using the changelog section it just dated as the brief. 'approve' pushes without asking - a wiki has no draft state, so that publishes immediately and irreversibly. Omitted behaves as 'ask' where the repo has a wiki, and does nothing where it does not.

protectedPaths.description: Extra files this project's agents must never hand-edit, on top of the shared defaults (.env, lockfiles, node_modules, build output, .git). Use for generated files a generator owns. Keeps language-specific rules out of the shared hook.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against the absolute path with forward slashes.

why.description: Shown in the denial. Say what owns the file, so the reader knows what to change instead.

trigger.description: 'draft-on-push' creates a draft release when the version changes on trunk; publishing the draft is a separate manual act.

prereleaseChannel.description: The VS Code Marketplace rejects SemVer prerelease identifiers outright, so a beta channel must use --pre-release on odd minors instead.

models.description: Model tier per pipeline phase. Cost is a tie-breaker only; intelligence wins on anything that ships.

ticketFirst.description: Work requires a tracker ticket before a worktree is claimed.

trivialEscape.description: Allow a declared-trivial change to skip ahead, filing a retroactive ticket at PR time.

agentsMayClose.description: Whether an agent may close tracker issues. False means label and comment only.

unprotectedPaths.description: Paths this project declares legitimately writable, SUBTRACTED from the shared defaults (.env, lockfiles, node_modules, build output). Use when a default is simply wrong here - `out/` is generated in most repos and is the deliverable in some. Cannot lift the .git/ rule. Without an escape like this, a wrong default does not prevent the write: it pushes it onto a shell command that no PreToolUse hook can observe.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against the absolute path with forward slashes.

why.description: Say why this path is legitimate output for this project. Read by humans reviewing the opt-out.

validation.description: Project-specific checks a ticket must pass before Build starts. A ticket can be coherent about this codebase and still ask for something the domain does not permit.

ticket.description: Run at Build step 1 against the ticket, and again at step 5 against the chosen approach.

name.description: Short label for the check, used when reporting which checks ran.

how.description: Instruction for performing it, naming the authority to consult - a skill, a document, or a command.

onFail.description: Where a failing ticket goes: capture to re-investigate, shape to be scoped, stop to report and halt.
